Every `before` was verified to occur verbatim in `file` at HEAD cdeb2d1 by the same audit probe X15 used. Each row names the test(s) that went red, with the assertion or log line quoted in the report. Run on maintainer-mac-1, 2026-10-31, lease F4-on9yl. The last 13 rows are fix round 1, run the same way against HEAD 2e76dc0 (lease F4-ral3b), and their `before` strings are read from the files as they ship at that commit. Round 0's row 6 (drop the `if:` on the restore step) was re-run at that commit too, and its `before` now records the text as it ships there.

notMutated.note: `the pinned action can talk to the CLI this repo installs` was not mutated: it compares the installed `react-native-harness/package.json` (version 1.6.0, `harnessActionProtocol: 1`) with `example/package.json`'s devDependency and the 40-char pin. Mutating it means editing node_modules or the pin, and the first `check` run after a dependency bump is the real failure mode; the case was verified to read real data by printing both sides.

`the release workflows still refuse to cancel a run that may be staging` guards what was already true (row 53's check), so it was run against the real files only. Its exactness (a literal `false`, not `'false'` or an expression) is deliberate and was confirmed by reading the parsed YAML.

`the list of ci subcommands still matches the installed CLI` is itself the drift guard: it was shown to work by deleting one entry from HARNESS_CI_SUBCOMMANDS in the scratch check while writing it, and it is the reason the ci-step excuse cannot widen silently.

Fix round 1 item 5 (the ledger, not the code) rests on evidence rather than mutation: the round-0 `harness:android` row whose log has no `gate: claimed …` line is the run launched without the lease env, and `claimDevicesFromEnv` (scripts/device-pool.mjs) returns null when no pair is named there. The fix is this branch's re-run under a lease, whose ledger row carries `lease: F4-ral3b` and the pair devices.

foundByCheck.note: The first `bun run check` on this branch was red for a reason no unit run had shown: the guard located the --clean help paragraph with /^\s+'  --clean/, but prettier had rewritten that literal with double quotes (its first line contains an apostrophe), so `expect(start).toBeGreaterThan(-1)` failed at 143 s. Both spellings are accepted now, and rows 19-20 above were re-run against the prettier-formatted source afterwards. A source-reading test must read the text, not one formatting of it.
